nativeUnits: Hartree atomic units throughout: total energies printed in Ha, lattice vectors and muffin-tin radii in bohr, reciprocal cutoffs in bohr^-1 — never Rydberg (the discriminating fact the census records by name).
strength: code identity is decisive
positives: Ground-state calculations were performed with the all-electron full-potential code Elk, using rgkmax = 8.
We used Elk (version 7.2), an FP-LAPW package, and all energies are in Hartree.
The Elk code solves the Kohn-Sham equations in atomic units, so the printed total energy is in Ha and the lattice vectors are in bohr.
negatives: A herd of elk crossed the plateau where the array is sited.
Unlike Elk, our all-electron implementation stores the density on a uniform radial grid.
census: §9 adjudication log, attribution fixes: "Elk is a Hartree-unit code (never Rydberg)" — the single code-identity fact the census already carries; §2.14 C157 asks for the table this row heads.
notes: Both atomic-unit keys are emitted because code identity fixes the MECHANICAL sector (ħ = m_e = e = 1) and says nothing about the EM rendering fork; "hartree" is the SI/4πε₀ rendering and "hartree-gaussian" the half-integer-charge rendering (same split detect.ts already makes with ATOMIC_FAMILY). Homograph guard: the animal is lowercase, so the pattern is case-sensitive and the cue is required.

nativeUnits: Rydberg atomic units internally (ħ = 2m_e = e²/2 = 1): pw.x prints the total energy in Ry and forces in Ry/bohr, cell and positions in bohr (or in alat units), while the post-processing executables (dos.x, projwfc.x, bands.x) print eV and ph.x prints cm^-1/THz — the Ry-vs-eV split ACROSS executables is the discriminator, not a switch.
strength: code identity plus a unit token

The PWscf total energy converged to 1e-8 Ry on a 12x12x12 k-point mesh.
Relaxations were run with pw.x until the residual forces fell below 1e-4 Ry/bohr.
negatives: For comparison with Quantum ESPRESSO we quote the same quantity in Ry.
Ref. [21] describes the Quantum ESPRESSO distribution for materials modelling.
census: §3 atomic-cm row "Solid-state and DFT practical units" (C42, C153: table BOTH dialects — VASP eV/Å and Quantum-ESPRESSO/abinit Ry/bohr); §3 "Rydberg atomic units" row for the generator set; §2.14 C157.
notes: Two layers must not be conflated: the code's INTERNAL convention is Rydberg atomic units (a registry row), while the Ry/bohr numbers a paper prints are also a display dialect (Cluster D). Emit "rydberg" for equations written in QE's own convention; a bare table of Ry numbers is a converter job, not a restoration.

implies.none: VASP's eV/Å practical units are numeric-only, Cluster D: no generator is absorbed (ħ, m_e, e all appear at full strength inside the code), so there is nothing to restore and no registry row applies. The census's "Solid-state and DFT practical units" row is deliberately class numeric-only; route to the converter (§2.9), not the translator.

census: §3 atomic-cm "Solid-state and DFT practical units (eV, Å, meV/atom, GPa, r.l.u.)" — class numeric-only, v1, with the C42/C153 instruction to table the VASP dialect separately; §6.2 Cluster D.

nativeUnits: Rydberg for energies, bohr for lengths: case.struct lattice parameters and muffin-tin radii in bohr, the SCF energy (:ENE) in Ry, convergence criteria in Ry per cell; densities of states and band plots are conventionally re-rendered in eV by the plotting tools.

nativeUnits: Atomic (Hartree) units internally — the ENERGY| lines print total energies in a.u. — while input keywords carry explicit bracketed unit tags ([eV], [angstrom]) whose ABSENCE means atomic units, with the notorious exception that the plane-wave CUTOFF is read in Ry by default.

nativeUnits: Hartree atomic units internally — "SCF Done: E(...) = ... A.U." — with input geometry in Å by default, harmonic frequencies in cm^-1, and thermochemistry printed in Hartree while relative energies are conventionally quoted in kcal/mol.

Both negatives are blocked by the pattern itself, not by the frame.

nativeUnits: Hartree atomic units: the FINAL SINGLE POINT ENERGY is in Eh and gradients in Eh/bohr, with input geometry in Å by default (an explicit bohr keyword switches it) and spectra printed in cm^-1 or eV.

nativeUnits: Hartree atomic units, like every coupled-cluster program: energies in Eh, geometry in Å at the input layer. implies.none: The census's GRMHD code-units row — c; G; M_BH; ε₀ (Heaviside–Lorentz), class quotient + riders, v2 — is NOT a registry row yet. nativeUnits: G = c = 1 with the black-hole mass as the length and time unit (GM/c² and GM/c³), and the magnetic field in Heaviside–Lorentz form so that the magnetic pressure is b²/2 with NO 4π; the density/accretion scale is a separately assigned ℳ_unit (M_unit) applied in post-processing, and is simply missing for scale-free runs.

nativeUnits: Dimensionless code units chosen per problem generator (no fixed physical scale), with the magnetic field defined so that the magnetic pressure is B²/2 and v_A = B/√ρ — i.e. the √4π already absorbed; the GR modules add G = c = M = 1 on top.

Compared with Athena++, our code adds radiation transport in code units.

nativeUnits: G = c = 1 with the mass unit conventionally M_⊙ (1 code length = 1.4766 km, 1 code time = 4.9255 μs, densities in M_⊙^-2 geometric units); many runs instead normalize to the total ADM mass M, which is bh-scale rather than nr-code — the QUOTED NUMBERS, not the equations, separate the two.

nativeUnits: G = c = 1 with the total mass M = 1: waveform times, radii and frequencies are in units of M, and the waveform is rescaled to a physical mass only when it is injected — the archetypal imported_artifact, since a strain "scaled to M = 74.6 M_⊙" names a convention it never declares.
strength: code identity plus a unit token

implies.none: Custom generators, not a registry row: the census's "GADGET / AREPO / GIZMO cosmological code units" backlog row is the triple [L] = h⁻¹kpc, [M] = 10¹⁰ h⁻¹M_⊙, [V] = km s⁻¹, which compounds with little-h INSIDE the mass unit. Nothing in CONVENTIONS carries a per-paper length/mass/velocity triple.

implies.none: Custom generators: RAMSES declares its scaling as three cgs conversion factors (units_d, units_l, units_t) in the namelist, which is the census's "Astrophysical simulation code-unit triples (G ≠ 1)" row — a per-paper generator set with no registry key.

nativeUnits: Dimensionless code units defined by the namelist triple units_d, units_l, units_t (density, length, time in cgs); cosmological runs conventionally scale the box to 1 and the density to the mean matter density, so a printed "density = 5" means 5 ρ̄ and the scale lives in the namelist, not the paper.
strength: code identity plus a unit token
positives: The AMR simulations were run with RAMSES; the namelist sets units_d, units_l and units_t for the cgs scaling.
RAMSES cosmological runs use boxlen = 1, so all lengths are in units of the box.
We used Ramses in code units, with densities normalized to the mean comoving matter density.

RAMSES is described in Ref. [70].
census: §3 per-paper nondimensionalization, "Astrophysical simulation code-unit triples (G ≠ 1)"; §6.5 cue (vi) code keywords.

Do not restore a RAMSES density without the namelist.

implies.none: Hénon (N-body standard) units — G = M_tot = 1 with E_tot = −1/4 — are a census row (§3, custom generators, v2) with NO registry key; the two numeric_factor conventions in the census (4·|E| vs −1/4·E) are unreconciled, so an encoder must pick and record one.

nativeUnits: Hénon / standard N-body units: G = 1, total cluster mass M = 1, total energy E = −1/4 (equivalently the virial radius = 1), so the crossing time is 2√2; physical times in Myr and masses in M_⊙ appear only through the scaling factors printed at the start of a run.
strength: code identity is decisive
cue: \bN-body units\b|\bH[eé]non units\b|\bG = M = 1\b|\bvirial radius\b|\bstar cluster\b|\bglobular\b|\bMyr\b|\bcrossing time\b|\bcode units\b
positives: The cluster models were integrated with NBODY6++ in standard N-body units, G = M = 1 and E = -1/4.
NBODY7 reports times in N-body units, with the physical scaling printed at the start of the run.
We used nbody6 for the globular-cluster runs, with the virial radius set to unity.
negatives: NBODY6 is compared with Monte Carlo methods in Ref. [9].
Nbody6 appears in the title of Ref. [9], which we cite for the integrator.
census: §3 gr-cosmo-astro "Hénon units (N-body units): G = M = 1, E = -1/4" and its nondim twin; §6.2 Cluster C ("the third normalization lives in prose, not equations; separators are quoted numbers — t_cr = 2√2"); §9 numeric erratum "Hénon-units c ~ 10⁴–10⁵".
notes: Cluster C is exactly the case this table exists for: the equations of a Newtonian G = 1 system are identical across three normalizations and the code name is the only discriminator. The second negative is blocked by the cue requirement, not by the pattern.

nativeUnits: Nothing until the input is read: `units lj` gives the reduced set (σ = ε = m = k_B = 1), `real` gives kcal/mol, Å, fs, K, atm, `metal` gives eV, Å, ps, K, bar, `si` and `cgs` are literal, and `electron` is the census's refuse-class hybrid (time fs vs a.u., mass amu vs m_e, velocity bohr per 1.03275 fs — inconsistent on three axes).
strength: weak: many codes allow unit switches, e.g. LAMMPS units real/metal/si/electron/lj must be read from the input
positives: The melt was simulated in LAMMPS with units lj, so lengths are in sigma and energies in epsilon.
All LAMMPS runs use reduced Lennard-Jones units with a cutoff of 2.5 sigma.
We ran LAMMPS in Lennard-Jones units; the time step is 0.005 tau.
negatives: The LAMMPS input specifies units metal, so energies are in eV and distances in Angstrom.
Unlike LAMMPS, our code has no unit-style switch and always uses reduced units.
census: §3 atomic-cm "Molecular-dynamics simulation unit sets (LAMMPS real/metal/electron, GROMACS, AMBER, reduced LJ)" — the `units electron` variant is refuse-class, the others are lookup-table custom generators; §7 refuse list (LAMMPS "units electron": "detection must never rest on two axes agreeing"); §6.5 cue (vi) `units lj`.
notes: The cue IS the rule here: the code name alone implies nothing, and the lj-reduced key is emitted only when the lj style is stated. The first negative is the important one — `units metal` is a live LAMMPS sentence that must NOT produce lj-reduced (it is eV/Å display units, Cluster D), and `units electron` must trigger the §7 refusal by name.

implies.none: GROMACS's fixed unit set (nm, ps, u, kJ/mol, e, K, bar) is a lookup-table custom-generator row in the census's MD unit-sets entry, and its molar energy needs N_A as a generator (the "Quantum-chemistry molar energy conventions" row). Neither is encoded in CONVENTIONS.

nativeUnits: A fixed, non-switchable set: length nm, time ps, mass u (amu), energy kJ/mol, charge e, temperature K, pressure bar — the nm (not Å) and kJ/mol (not kcal/mol) pair is the fastest discriminator against AMBER/NAMD/CHARMM outputs.
strength: code identity is decisive
positives: MD was run with GROMACS; the box was 5 nm on a side and energies are in kJ/mol.
Gromacs trajectories are written in nm and ps, with masses in amu.
All GROMACS simulations used the CHARMM36 force field at 1 bar.
negatives: Compared with GROMACS, our integrator is slower per ns of trajectory.
GROMACS is cited as Ref. [12].
census: §3 atomic-cm "Molecular-dynamics simulation unit sets"; §3 "Quantum-chemistry molar energy conventions (kcal mol⁻¹, kJ mol⁻¹, eV)" — generator N_A, custom generators, v1.
notes: The kJ/mol energy is the interesting half: a per-mole energy carries N_A as a genuine generator (the census gives it its own row), so this is not merely a display rescaling of SI. Second negative is blocked by ANTI_FRAME only.

implies.none: Same census row as GROMACS (MD unit sets, lookup-table custom generators) plus the molar-energy N_A row; no registry key.

nativeUnits: Å, kcal/mol, amu, e, with the internal time unit 1/20.455 ps ≈ 48.888 fs = √(amu·Å²/(kcal mol⁻¹)) — so a raw internal "time" is neither fs nor ps, and the printed trajectory times are already converted.
strength: code identity is decisive
positives: The trajectories were produced with AMBER using the ff14SB force field; energies are in kcal/mol and lengths in Angstrom.
AMBER's pmemd module was used with a 2 fs time step and a 9 Å cutoff.
All AMBER free energies are given in kcal/mol.
negatives: The sample was embedded in amber and imaged at 5 keV.
Unlike AMBER, our force field is polarizable, with energies in kcal/mol.
census: §3 atomic-cm "Molecular-dynamics simulation unit sets (… GROMACS, AMBER, reduced LJ)"; §3 molar-energy row.
notes: FLAGGED: the 20.455 internal time factor (TIMFAC) is from memory; the number is self-consistent — √(amu·Å²/(kcal/mol)) = 48.888 fs = 1/20.455 ps — which is why I kept it, but verify before it is used to convert a raw internal time. The Å/kcal/mol part is safe.

implies.none: The census's "Gyrokinetic normalization, GENE / c_s family" row (L_ref; c_ref = √(T_ref/m_ref); T_ref; m_ref; n_ref; e; B_ref — quotient + riders, v2) is not encoded in CONVENTIONS.

nativeUnits: L_ref (the major radius R₀ or the minor radius a), the reference sound speed c_ref = √(T_ref/m_ref) with NO factor of √2, plus T_ref (energy units, k_B = 1), m_ref, n_ref, B_ref; growth rates and frequencies come out in c_ref/L_ref and lengths in ρ_ref = c_ref m_ref/(eB_ref).
strength: code identity is decisive
positives: The gyrokinetic simulations were carried out with GENE in a flux-tube geometry.
GENE normalizes lengths to the major radius and speeds to c_s = sqrt(T_e/m_i), with no factor of sqrt(2).
Linear growth rates from GENE are given in units of c_s/a for the tokamak case.
negatives: The gene encoding the protein was silenced in the control sample.
The GENE results are compared with the experimental growth rates in Fig. 4.
census: §3 per-paper nondimensionalization, "Gyrokinetic normalization, GENE / c_s family"; §2.14 C76 (a display-normalization layer: 1004.0279 integrates in a₀/v_th0 and reports frequencies in ω_A = k_∥v_A — "it defeats an extractor that has correctly read the code declaration").
notes: Homograph guard: "gene" the biology word is lowercase, so the pattern is case-sensitive AND the cue is required — an all-caps GENE inside a genomics acronym would still need a gyrokinetic/plasma token. The √2 ABSENCE is the whole discriminating content of this row; it is only meaningful against the GS2 row below.

implies.none: The census's "Gyrokinetic normalization, GS2 / stella / AstroGK family" row (a; √2·v_t,r = √(2T_r/m_r); T_r; m_r; n_r; B_r) is not a registry row — and the round-5 kernel audit found its recorded 6-generator set has rank 4 (same-dimension reference scales), so it needs an anisotropy/symmetry flag before it can be encoded at all.

nativeUnits: Same axes as GENE but the reference speed carries the √2: v_t,r = √(2T_r/m_r), with a = the minor radius; a frequency quoted "in units of v_t/a" therefore differs from GENE's "c_s/a" by exactly √2 at identical physics.
strength: code identity is decisive
positives: The gyrokinetic runs used GS2 with the thermal speed v_t = sqrt(2T/m).
AstroGK evolves the same normalized equations, with frequencies in units of v_t/a for the plasma case.
We used stella, a flux-tube gyrokinetic code, for the stellarator geometry.
negatives: Per aspera ad astra: the stella of the emblem is unrelated to the instrument.
Unlike GS2, our code uses a full-f formulation in a flux tube.
census: §3 "Gyrokinetic normalization, GS2 / stella / AstroGK family" with the round-5 kernel-audit note (rank 4, the C34 direction-split-length issue in executable form); §2.14 C09 (1004.0279 drops its hats with no marker) and C76; §6.2 conflicting fingerprints (1004.0279 is SI in the main text and Gaussian-CGS in an inherited appendix).
notes: The √2 fork against GENE is the census's own recorded fact, which is why confidence is higher here than for most code-identity rows. "stella" is lowercase in its own name, so the pattern uses a lookahead cue instead of capitalization.

nativeUnits: Internally c = 1 with Mpc as BOTH the length and the time unit — conformal time τ and 1/H in Mpc, wavenumbers in Mpc⁻¹ — while outputs are optionally re-rendered in h/Mpc and (Mpc/h)³; ħ and k_B are NOT absorbed (neutrino masses stay in eV, temperatures in K).
strength: code identity plus a unit token
positives: The linear power spectra were computed with CLASS, which works in Mpc units with c = 1.
We modified CLASS to add an extra Boltzmann hierarchy for the dark sector.
CMB spectra from CLASS agree with CAMB to better than 0.1%.
negatives: Objects in this class are unaffected by the rescaling.
CLASS A stars were excluded from the sample before stacking.
census: §3 gr-cosmo-astro "Observational cosmology hybrid units (km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, Mpc, M_⊙, K, eV)" — numeric-only, Cluster D — plus "Little-h units"; §6.2 Cluster D; §2.14 C25 (data-product imports are the norm in cosmology).
notes: FLAGGED — the weakest mapping in the table. c = 1 is genuinely absorbed (H in Mpc⁻¹ requires it), which is why "c-only" is emitted, but the Mpc scale and the h-branch on top of it are DISPLAY units (Cluster D) that c-only does not describe, and I have not verified from the CLASS source that no other constant is absorbed. If in doubt, downgrade this row to a none-entry naming §3's observational-cosmology row.

nativeUnits: Same convention as CLASS: c = 1 with Mpc as the length and conformal-time unit, k in Mpc⁻¹, with h-scaled output available; masses and temperatures stay in eV and K, so ħ and k_B are explicit.
strength: code identity plus a unit token
positives: Linear transfer functions were generated with CAMB on a grid of k in Mpc^-1.
We used CAMB for the CMB power spectra and the matter power spectrum at z = 0.
CAMB and CLASS were run with identical cosmological parameters.
negatives: Compared with CAMB, our Boltzmann solver is slower by an order of magnitude.
CAMB is described in Ref. [3].
census: §3 "Observational cosmology hybrid units" and "Little-h units"; §6.2 Cluster D.
notes: FLAGGED with the same caveat as CLASS: the c = 1 + Mpc pair is a code fact I believe but did not verify here, and the h-branch is a separate axis (§3's little-h row, whose absolute-magnitude sign the census had to correct to −5 log h).

nativeUnits: SI at the library boundary: waveform generators take masses in kilograms, distance in metres and times in seconds (GPS), and return dimensionless strain — while the numerical-relativity waveforms the library ingests are in G = c = M = 1 code units, so the SI/code-unit seam sits INSIDE the pipeline.
strength: code identity plus a unit token
positives: Waveforms were generated with LALSimulation, whose interfaces take masses in kg and distances in metres.
The IMRPhenomXPHM approximant from LALSuite was used for the strain model.
We call LALInference through its Python bindings for the SEOBNRv4 waveform.
negatives: Unlike LALSuite, our pipeline stores masses in solar units throughout.
The lal directory contains the build scripts for the pipeline.
census: §2.14 C25 (an imported_artifact span class — "data-product imports are the norm in GW, cosmology and lattice, each with its own unstated span"); §6.4 ("constants-explicit SI is positively assertible"); §6.5b's ranked equation-form recovery for GW (PSD sidedness, Fourier kernel, ΔL/L vs δL/L, F₊/F×, detector-frame).
notes: This row's value is the SEAM, not the SI claim: a paper that says "LALSimulation" and quotes masses in M_⊙ is running SI internals behind a solar-mass display layer, and the NR waveform it injected carries a third convention (G = c = M = 1) that nobody declared. FLAGGED: the kg/metre API convention is from memory of the LALSimulation signatures.

implies.none: Solar masses, Mpc, seconds and Hz are Cluster D display units — zero generators, nothing to restore — sitting on top of LAL's SI internals. The census's "Observational cosmology hybrid units" and "Stellar and solar reference units" rows are both numeric-only; no registry key applies.

nativeUnits: Priors, samples and posteriors in M_⊙ (detector-frame unless stated), luminosity distance in Mpc, times in GPS seconds, frequencies in Hz — a display layer over LALSimulation's SI calls; the detector-frame/source-frame mass distinction is a FRAME identity tag, not a unit.
strength: code identity plus a unit token
positives: Parameter estimation was run with bilby using uniform priors in chirp mass and a luminosity distance in Mpc.
PyCBC quotes component masses in solar masses and distances in Mpc.
The posteriors from bilby and PyCBC agree for GW150914.
negatives: The bilby is a nocturnal marsupial with a long snout.
Compared with PyCBC, our search has a lower false-alarm rate.
census: §6.2 Cluster D (display units: nothing to restore, but converter work remains); §2.14 C25; §2.13/§6.5b frame tags ("detector-frame" → frame tag).
notes: The detector-frame vs source-frame mass fork is the highest-damage identity tag in this row and is NOT a unit conversion — it is a redshift-dependent relabelling, so it must be surfaced as an identity tag, never absorbed into a factor.

nativeUnits: Lattice units a = 1 on top of ħ = c = 1: every printed mass is the dimensionless product am, the coupling enters as β = 6/g₀², and the action is Euclidean — the scale is set afterwards by a separate scale-setting quantity (r₀, w₀, f_π), which is where the physical units actually enter.
strength: code identity is decisive
positives: The gauge configurations were generated with the MILC code at beta = 6.3 on 32^3 x 64 lattices.
Propagators were computed with Chroma using domain-wall fermions.
We used QUDA for the multi-GPU solver on the same lattice ensembles.
negatives: The chroma subcarrier sits at 4.43 MHz in the analogue signal.
Unlike MILC, our ensembles use stout smearing on the same lattice.
census: §3 hep-natural "Lattice units (a = 1) on top of ħ = c = 1" (custom generators, v1); §6.4 strong tokens (am_π or β = 6/g₀² → lattice); §7 refuse list (Euclidean↔Minkowski continuation: tag it Euclidean per §2.12, NEVER continue it); §2.14 C25 (lattice data-product imports).
notes: Two obligations travel with this key and neither is a unit: the Euclidean tag (§7 refuses continuation outright) and the scale-setting quantity, without which am is not convertible to MeV. Emitting "lattice" alone would be an incomplete answer.

implies.none: Mechanical cgs is a pure unit-magnitude rescaling of SI — numeric-only, zero generators, nothing to restore (the census's class for the whole historical/engineering family). The solar-unit reports (M_⊙, R_⊙, L_⊙) are the separate "Stellar and solar reference units" numeric-only row, where GM_⊙ is stored as primary.

nativeUnits: cgs throughout — inlist parameters and the internal star structure in g, cm, s, erg, K, with log g in cgs — while the reported quantities are conventionally in M_⊙, R_⊙, L_⊙; every constant (G, c, a_rad, k_B) appears explicitly, so this is a POSITIVE zero-generator assertion, not an absence of evidence.
strength: code identity is decisive
cue: \bstellar evolution\b|\bModules for Experiments in Stellar Astrophysics\b|\binlists?\b|\bZAMS\b|\b(?:M_sun|M_\\?odot|solar mass(?:es)?)\b|\bmetallicit\w+\b|\bcgs\b|\bmain sequence\b|\bopacit\w+\b
positives: The stellar models were computed with MESA at metallicity Z = 0.014.
MESA works internally in cgs, and the inlist parameters are given in g, cm and s.
We evolved a 20 M_sun star from ZAMS with MESA using the standard opacity tables.
negatives: The array sits on a mesa at 2550 m elevation.
Compared with MESA, our one-zone model omits rotation in cgs units.
census: §6.4 ("Constants-explicit SI is positively assertible, not the residue of nothing firing" — the same rule in its cgs rendering); §3 "Stellar and solar reference units (M_⊙, R_⊙, L_⊙; IAU nominal values)" — numeric-only, store GM_⊙ as primary (T9); §6.2 Cluster D.
notes: Homograph: "mesa" the landform, and MESA the graphics library — case-sensitivity plus the astrophysical cue handles both. The engine should emit "cgs, asserted" here, distinctly from "no fingerprints fired".

implies.none: cgs (or MKS) with every constant explicit: a numeric-only unit-magnitude choice with zero generators, selected at runtime by the UnitSystem parameter, so there is no registry row and no restoration to perform — only converter work.

nativeUnits: Runtime-selected unit system (a UnitSystem parameter, CGS by default with MKS available) and all physical constants carried explicitly; the astrophysical setups additionally scale lengths to the domain size, which is a per-problem custom generator on top.
strength: weak: the unit system is a runtime parameter (CGS default, MKS available), so it must be read from the parameter file rather than inferred from the code name
positives: The hydrodynamic simulations used the FLASH code with adaptive mesh refinement in cgs units.
FLASH4 was run with the UnitSystem parameter left at its CGS default.
All FLASH simulations of the supernova shock use cgs units throughout.
negatives: The FLASH free-electron laser at DESY delivers 30 fs pulses.
Compared with FLASH, our code includes radiation transport in cgs units.
